// NEGATIVE fixture — bare builtin specifiers only.
//
// This check runs against the RAW source on purpose: what it bans *is* a string literal, so
// stripping strings and comments would blank the very text it looks for. The price is deliberate
// over-strictness — it also fires when a comment or a string writes a prefixed specifier out in
// full after an import keyword. That is why the near-misses below never spell one out.
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

const SCHEME = 'node:';

export function read(p) {
  return fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(p), 'utf-8');
}

export function stripScheme(spec) {
  const s = String(spec);
  return s.indexOf(SCHEME) === 0 ? s.slice(SCHEME.length) : s;
}

export { SCHEME };
